crime: {WITCH_NAME} always had bruises or scars, though no one ever saw her get hurt. A girl spent evenings reading beside her under the library's unwilting cherry tree. Once, seeing a fresh wound on her wrist, the girl simply pulled her sleeve down over it.

One evening, alone with her in the library, the girl rose with her books, slipped, and struck the back of her head on a bookshelf's corner. No one had touched her. {WITCH_NAME} caught her too late and held her as she died.

Before the others arrived, {WITCH_NAME} rolled up her sleeves and made deep grip-shaped bruises and a long scratch appear on her arms. She was still holding the body when the girls found her. “It was me,” she said.

They took the head wound for a blow and the marks on her arms for signs of a dying struggle. She confirmed they had been alone and never withdrew her confession. She blamed herself for failing to save the girl and accepted the rest as hers as well.
fields.epitaph: She signed for a crime she had never committed.
fields.epithet: A Verdict Written on Her Skin
execution: An iron frame held her upright with her scarred arms spread bare. A spike pointed at her chest. As a guard read the sentence, the frame turned a screw, driving the spike farther forward with each phrase. On the final word, it drove through her chest.

magic.name: the Written Wound
magic.text: She can create any real wound she chooses on her own body.
